taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: OIDC front/back-channel logout and local session termination
controls.source_trace: Trace issuer/session identity from a logout message to exactly the intended local sessions. Inspect replay and whether a notification merely clears UI state.
controls.implementation_branch: Back-channel logout validation and front-channel browser state are different paths. Resolve sid/sub and issuer/client binding before selecting sessions. Browser cookie restrictions may block front-channel effects; a local logout UI change is not evidence that a server session or refresh family ended.
controls.operational_method: Validate a back-channel logout token as its own token class: signature/context, required logout event, issuer/audience, time and sid/sub selection; reject a Logout Token containing any nonce claim, even with an otherwise valid signature/events object. A valid login ID token is not a Logout Token. Retain replay handling and the exact selected sessions. Compare an authentic synthetic logout token with an otherwise valid login ID token and a wrong-session token; UI logout alone proves no refresh-family revocation.
controls.controlled_verification: Use two owned issuer sessions and local sessions; compare intended logout, wrong-issuer/session message and a harmless replay.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A changed login screen is not proof that a server session was revoked; global logout may be an intentional policy rather than overbroad binding.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Validate logout issuer/context and revoke the correct sessions; retest retained unrelated sessions and intended termination.
